name: Facial Aging Consistency
description: Analyzes consistency of aging features (wrinkles, spots, skin texture) across face — AI often has inconsistent aging.
mechanism:
This method checks facial aging consistency for deepfake detection:

1. **Age Marker Detection**: Facial aging markers are detected per frame: wrinkle density and depth (crow's feet, forehead lines, nasolabial folds), skin texture changes (reduced elasticity, increased roughness), skin laxity (jowling, under-eye bags), and pigmentation changes.

2. **Age Consistency Verification**: All aging markers should indicate a consistent age range. The method checks whether wrinkle density, skin texture, and facial volume are mutually consistent. Deepfakes that swap faces between individuals of different ages may produce inconsistent aging cues — young skin texture with deep wrinkles, or aged skin with juvenile facial volume.

3. **Regional Age Coherence**: Different facial regions should show coherent aging. The method verifies that forehead wrinkles, crow's feet, nasolabial folds, and neck skin show the same approximate aging level. AI generation may produce faces with regionally inconsistent aging — perfectly smooth forehead with aged eye areas.

4. **Temporal Aging Stability**: Aging markers are static structures that don't change between video frames. Wrinkle positions and depths should remain constant. The method tracks aging markers across frames — deepfake generators may produce temporally inconsistent wrinkles that appear, disappear, or shift position as the face is re-generated each frame.

5. **Context-Face Age Matching**: If the surrounding context provides age cues (body, hands, clothing style), the method checks whether the face age is consistent with these contextual indicators. Face-swapping an young face onto an older body creates detectable age inconsistencies between face and body.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
